name: Brian Acton
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Acton graduated Stanford in 1994 and worked as a systems administrator and product tester at Rockwell, Apple, and Adobe before joining Yahoo in 1996 as the 44th employee. WhatsApp was co-founded in 2009 at age 37.
early_history_summary: Acton grew up in Michigan and Central Florida, graduated from Lake Howell High School, and attended Stanford on a full scholarship, graduating in 1994 with a CS degree. He worked at Rockwell, Apple, and Adobe before joining Yahoo in 1996.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Michigan, later moving to Central Florida. Received a full scholarship to study engineering at the University of Pennsylvania before transferring to Stanford.
evidence_summary: Acton received a full scholarship to Stanford and graduated with a CS degree in 1994, then worked at several tech companies before joining Yahoo in 1996. No material founding or achievement milestone occurred by age 26; his major success came with WhatsApp in 2009 at age 37.

name: Jan Koum
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Koum immigrated to the US at 16, worked as a cleaner and security tester, and joined Yahoo as an infrastructure engineer in 1997. WhatsApp was co-founded in 2009 at age 33. Note: CSV lists birth year as 1970, but Wikipedia and Forbes confirm 1976.
early_history_summary: Born in Kyiv, Ukraine to a Jewish family, Koum moved to Mountain View, California at age 16 with his mother. He worked as a grocery store cleaner while his mother babysat. He became interested in programming by age 18, enrolled at San Jose State University, and worked at Ernst & Young as a security tester before joining Yahoo in 1997.
family_context_summary: Born to a Jewish family in Kyiv; father was a construction manager who built hospitals and schools; mother was a housewife. Family immigrated to Mountain View, CA when Koum was 16, living in a small apartment with social support. Father died in Ukraine in 1997 and mother died of cancer in 2000.
evidence_summary: Koum immigrated from Ukraine to Mountain View at 16 in poverty, worked menial jobs, and taught himself programming. He joined Yahoo in 1997 and worked there for nine years. No material founding or achievement milestone occurred by age 26; WhatsApp was co-founded in 2009 at age 33.

name: Ben Silbermann
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Silbermann graduated Yale in 2003, worked as a consultant, then joined Google in 2006 in online advertising. Pinterest launched in March 2010 at age 27.
early_history_summary: Born in Iowa to ophthalmologist parents, Silbermann attended the Research Science Institute at MIT in 1998 and graduated from Yale in 2003 with a degree in Political Science. He worked as a consultant, then joined Google's online advertising group in 2006 before leaving to start his own iPhone apps.
family_context_summary: Born in Des Moines, Iowa; parents are ophthalmologists; both sisters are also doctors. Middle-class to upper-middle-class professional family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents are ophthalmologists; no direct technology domain expertise in the family.
evidence_summary: Silbermann grew up in Iowa in a medical family, attended Yale, and worked at Google before founding Pinterest. No material founding or achievement milestone occurred by age 26; Pinterest launched in March 2010 at age 27.

name: Jack Dorsey
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Dorsey wrote dispatch software as a teenager and started a small dispatch company in Oakland in 2000, but it failed during the dot-com crash. Twitter was co-founded in 2006 at age 29.
early_history_summary: Born in St. Louis, Missouri, Dorsey became interested in dispatch routing by age 14 and wrote dispatch software as a teenager. He attended University of Missouri-Rolla, then transferred to NYU but dropped out. He moved to California and started a dispatch company in 2000, which failed. He then bounced between contract programming jobs before joining Odeo in 2006.
family_context_summary: Born to a middle-class family in St. Louis; father was an engineer who developed mass spectrometers; mother was a homemaker. Raised Catholic.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father worked for a company that developed mass spectrometers, providing some engineering/technical environment in the home.
evidence_summary: Dorsey showed early programming talent, writing dispatch software as a teenager, and started a dispatch company at 23-24, but it failed. No material milestone occurred by age 26; Twitter was co-founded in 2006 at age 29.

name: Biz Stone
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Stone worked as a book cover designer at Little, Brown and Company and was creative director at Xanga from 1999 to 2001. Twitter was co-founded in 2006 at age 32. Being an employee at Xanga is not a material founding or achievement milestone.
early_history_summary: Born in Boston, Stone attended Northeastern University and UMass Boston but did not graduate. He started his career moving boxes at Little, Brown and Company, became a book cover designer, then served as creative director at Xanga (1999-2001) before joining Google's Blogger team in 2003.
family_context_summary: Born in Boston, Massachusetts. Not much documented about family background beyond this.
evidence_summary: Stone dropped out of college, became a book cover designer, and served as creative director at Xanga by his mid-20s. No material founding or achievement milestone occurred by age 26; Twitter was co-founded in 2006 at age 32.

name: Evan Williams
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Pyra Labs on January 1, 1999 at age 26, which created Blogger, one of the first and most influential blog-publishing platforms.
early_history_summary: Williams grew up on a farm in Clarks, Nebraska, and attended the University of Nebraska-Lincoln for 1.5 years before leaving. He worked various tech jobs in Florida and Texas, then moved to Sebastopol, California in 1996 to work for O'Reilly Media, where he learned to code and began blogging on EvHead.com. In January 1999, he co-founded Pyra Labs with Meg Hourihan.
family_context_summary: Grew up on a farm in Clarks, Nebraska (population ~379); parents were Laurie Howe and Monte Williams; assisted with crop irrigation during summers.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; family was in farming, not technology.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught programmer, early blogger, Silicon Valley proximity, dot-com wave, O'Reilly Media network
evidence_summary: Williams grew up on a farm in rural Nebraska with no technology background in his family. He dropped out of college, worked various tech jobs, and moved to California in 1996 to work at O'Reilly Media, where he learned to code and began blogging. His own experience as a blogger gave him direct domain proximity when he co-founded Pyra Labs in January 1999 at age 26, which created Blogger. He rode the dot-com and blogging wave, and benefited from his Silicon Valley ecosystem proximity and complementary co-founder Meg Hourihan. No family wealth, elite institution, or inherited network is documented.
starting_point: Born to a farming family in Clarks, Nebraska (population ~379); grew up on a farm assisting with crop irrigation; parents had no technology background.
current_position: Co-founder of Obvious Ventures; net worth estimated at ~$2 billion as of 2025; previously co-founded Twitter, Blogger, and Medium.

trajectory.event: Moved to Sebastopol, California to work for O'Reilly Media; began blogging on EvHead.com and learning to code.
Co-founded Pyra Labs with Meg Hourihan on January 1; launched Blogger, one of the first blog-publishing platforms.
Pyra Labs and Blogger acquired by Google for an undisclosed sum.
Co-founded Twitter via Obvious Corporation with Jack Dorsey and Biz Stone.
Became CEO of Twitter, succeeding Jack Dorsey.
Founded Medium, an online publishing platform.
Co-founded Obvious Ventures, a venture capital firm focused on world-positive companies.
Stepped down from Twitter board of directors.

name: Noah Glass
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Twitter in 2006 at age 24-25 within Odeo; coined the name 'Twitter' and helped design core features before being ousted later that year.
early_history_summary: Glass worked at Industrial Light & Magic and on projects with Marc Canter (Macromedia founder) before developing AudBlog, an audio blogging app. AudBlog was merged into a partnership with Evan Williams to create Odeo, a podcasting company. In 2006, within Odeo, Glass helped create and develop the concept for Twitter, coined its name, and was pushed out later that year by Williams.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Wikipedia does not list birthplace or family background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Evan Williams collaboration, Silicon Valley, Marc Canter mentorship, AudBlog experience
evidence_summary: Glass's early life and family background are not documented in reviewed sources. He worked at Industrial Light & Magic and with Marc Canter before developing AudBlog, which led to a partnership with Evan Williams and the creation of Odeo. Within Odeo in 2006, Glass co-founded Twitter, coined its name, and helped design core features. His primary advantage was his high-trust collaboration with Evan Williams, who brought Blogger experience and capital, and his Silicon Valley ecosystem proximity. Glass was ousted from Twitter in 2006 and subsequently maintained a low public profile. Documentation is limited; Wikipedia article is a stub.
current_position: Current status not widely documented; was ousted from Twitter in 2006 and subsequently maintained a low public profile.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Odeo, a podcasting company, with Evan Williams after his AudBlog startup merged with Williams' operation.
Co-founded Twitter within Odeo; coined the name 'Twitter' and helped design core features.
Ousted from Twitter by Evan Williams, who acquired Odeo's assets and renamed it Obvious Corporation.

name: Chad Hurley
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Hurley graduated from Indiana University of Pennsylvania in 1999 with a BA in Fine Art, joined PayPal as its first graphic designer, and designed the PayPal logo. He left PayPal in 2002 to freelance. YouTube was co-founded in February 2005 at age 28.
early_history_summary: Born in Reading, Pennsylvania, Hurley showed interest in arts and computers from childhood. He graduated from Twin Valley High School in 1995 and earned a BA in Fine Art from Indiana University of Pennsylvania in 1999. He joined PayPal as its first graphic designer, creating the PayPal logo during his interview, and left in 2002 to freelance.
family_context_summary: Born in Reading, Pennsylvania; parents are Don and Joann Hurley; father's occupation not specified in reviewed sources. Grew up near Birdsboro, Pennsylvania.
evidence_summary: Hurley studied fine art, joined PayPal as its first graphic designer in 1999, and designed the PayPal logo. While notable, this is a job task, not a material founding or achievement milestone. YouTube was co-founded in February 2005 at age 28.

name: Reed Hastings
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Hastings graduated from Bowdoin College in 1983, joined the Peace Corps (1983-1985) teaching math in Swaziland, then enrolled at Stanford for computer science in 1985. Pure Software was founded in 1991 at age 31. Netflix was founded in 1998 at age 38.
early_history_summary: Born in Boston, Massachusetts, Hastings attended Buckingham Browne & Nichols School in Cambridge. He graduated from Bowdoin College in 1983 with a math degree, spent two years in the Peace Corps in Swaziland, then earned a master's in computer science from Stanford in 1988. He worked as a software developer before founding Pure Software in 1991.
family_context_summary: Born in Boston; father was an attorney for the Department of Health, Education and Welfare in the Nixon administration; mother was a debutante from a Boston Brahmin family. Maternal great-grandfather was Alfred Lee Loomis, a prominent scientist and financier.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a government attorney; mother came from a Boston Brahmin family. No direct technology domain expertise, but family had strong educational and social connections.
evidence_summary: Hastings came from an affluent Boston family with deep connections (maternal great-grandfather was Alfred Lee Loomis). He graduated from Bowdoin, served in the Peace Corps, and earned a Stanford CS master's by 1988. No material founding or achievement milestone occurred by age 26; Pure Software was founded in 1991 at age 31 and Netflix in 1998 at age 38.

name: Pierre Omidyar
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Ink Development Corp (later eShop Inc.) on May 10, 1991 at age 23, an early pioneer of online shopping software later acquired by Microsoft in 1996.
early_history_summary: Born in Paris to Iranian parents, Omidyar moved to Maryland as a child when his father began a residency at Johns Hopkins. He became interested in computers in high school, wrote his first program at age 14, and graduated from Tufts University in 1988 with a CS degree. He worked at Claris (Apple subsidiary) before co-founding Ink Development Corp in May 1991.
family_context_summary: Born in Paris to Iranian parents; father was a physician who did residency at Johns Hopkins; mother was a linguistics academic who earned her doctorate at the Sorbonne; maternal grandfather was General Mahmud Mir-Djalali of the Imperial Iranian Army.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not in technology; father was a physician, mother was a linguistics academic. No direct tech domain expertise transferred.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early programming, CS degree Tufts, Claris experience, Silicon Valley, e-commerce pioneer, pen computing wave
evidence_summary: Omidyar was born in Paris to Iranian parents and moved to the US as a child. His father was a physician and his mother an academic, providing a stable middle-class background but no technology domain expertise. He showed early programming aptitude, writing his first program at 14, and graduated from Tufts with a CS degree in 1988. Working at Claris gave him Silicon Valley exposure and software product experience. He co-founded Ink Development Corp (later eShop) in May 1991 at age 23, riding the early e-commerce and pen computing wave. His technical depth in a scarce domain and early start in programming were his primary advantages. No significant inherited wealth, audience, or elite network is documented beyond his professional family background.
starting_point: Born in Paris to Iranian parents; father was a physician who completed residency at Johns Hopkins; mother was a linguistics academic; maternal grandfather was a general in the Imperial Iranian Army; family moved to Maryland and later Hawaii.
current_position: Philanthropist and founder of eBay; net worth estimated at ~$12 billion as of 2025; focuses on Omidyar Network and First Look Media; resides in Hawaii.

trajectory.event: Graduated from Tufts University with a degree in computer science; joined Claris, an Apple subsidiary, developing Macintosh software.
Co-founded Ink Development Corp (later eShop Inc.) on May 10, an early online shopping software company.
Launched AuctionWeb (later eBay) on Labor Day weekend as a side project on his personal website.
eShop acquired by Microsoft on June 11; quit his day job at General Magic to focus on eBay full-time.
eBay went public; Omidyar became a billionaire shortly after the IPO.
Founded Omidyar Network, a philanthropic investment firm.
Founded First Look Media, including The Intercept news organization.

name: Larry Ellison
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Ellison dropped out of University of Illinois and University of Chicago, moved to Berkeley in 1966, and bounced between programming jobs at Fireman's Fund, Wells Fargo, and Amdahl for the next decade. Oracle was co-founded in 1977 at age 33.
early_history_summary: Born in New York City to a single mother who gave him up for adoption, Ellison was raised in Chicago by his aunt and uncle. He attended the University of Illinois but dropped out after his sophomore year when his adoptive mother died. He then attended the University of Chicago for one semester before dropping out. He moved to Berkeley, California in 1966 and worked as a programmer at various companies for about a decade.
family_context_summary: Born to a single mother in New York; given up for adoption at 9 months to his mother's aunt and uncle in Chicago; adoptive father had lost his real estate business in the Great Depression and worked as an auditor for the public housing authority; raised in a two-bedroom apartment on the South Side.
parent_family_domain_summary: Adoptive father was an auditor for the public housing authority; no technology domain expertise in the family.
evidence_summary: Ellison was given up for adoption and raised in a lower-middle-class family in Chicago. He showed aptitude for math and science but dropped out of two colleges. He moved to Berkeley in 1966 and worked as a programmer at various companies for about a decade. No material founding or achievement milestone occurred by age 26; Oracle was co-founded in 1977 at age 33.

name: Tom Anderson
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Anderson was a teenage hacker (FBI raid at 14 in 1985) and studied English at UC Berkeley and film at UCLA. He worked as a product tester at XDrive in 2000. MySpace was co-founded in 2003 at age 33.
early_history_summary: Born in San Diego, California, Anderson was a computer hacker as a teenager under the pseudonym 'Lord Flathead,' prompting an FBI raid at 14 after hacking into Chase Manhattan Bank. He attended UC Berkeley majoring in English and rhetoric, was in a band, lived in Taiwan, then studied film at UCLA. He worked as a product tester at XDrive in 2000 before co-founding MySpace in 2003.
family_context_summary: Born in San Diego, California; father was an entrepreneur. Specific family financial status not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an entrepreneur; specific domain not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Anderson was a notable teenage hacker (FBI raid at 14) but spent his 20s studying English and film, playing in a band, and living in Taiwan. No material founding or achievement milestone occurred by age 26; MySpace was co-founded in 2003 at age 33.
